title: Coefficient squares for dense refinements and schematic closures
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be any of the coefficient maps specified in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image]: a homomorphism of finite commutative $\ell$-primary rings, $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ or $E\to F$ for finite $F/E$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, $\mathcal O_E\to E$, $E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a continuous map $\mathcal O_E\to A$ to a finite admissible ring, or a finite composite. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring; use pulled-back condensed coefficients, including the finite-subextension condensed convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Work in ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories on the small pro-étale sites [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $T_V=\Lambda'_V\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_V}-$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], $\gamma_{v,M}:T Rv_*M\to Rv_*TM$ for the unit/pullback/counit comparison [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image], and $\delta_{a,M}:T a_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}a_!TM$ for the canonical open comparison [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso, det-prop-scalar-six-pullback]. The notation $\Dctf$ means bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Let $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow Z,p:Z\to Y)$ and $c'=(j':X\hookrightarrow Z',p':Z'\to Y)$ be compactifications [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], and let $h:Z'\to Z$ be proper with $hj'=j$, $p'=ph$ and $h^{-1}(j(X))=j'(X)$. Assume either (a) both compactifications are dense, or (b) $Z'$ is the schematic closure of $X$ in $Z$ and $h$ is its closed inclusion. For $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ let $e_{h,K}:j_!K\to Rh_*j'_!K$ be the open-adjunction transpose of the inverse of the canonical identification $j^*Rh_*j'_!K\simeq K$. In case (a) this is the refinement map of [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement]; in case (b) it is the restriction-normalized schematic-closure identification of [sk-lem-nagata-density-normalization]. It is an isomorphism in both cases. Then
$$Rh_*\delta_{j',K}\circ\gamma_{h,j'_!K}\circ T_Z(e_{h,K})=e_{h,T_XK}\circ\delta_{j,K}.$$
Define $C_{c,K}=Rp_*\delta_{j,K}\circ\gamma_{p,j_!K}$ and $C_{c',K}=Rp'_*\delta_{j',K}\circ\gamma_{p',j'_!K}$, and put $\phi_{h,K}=Rp_*e_{h,K}$, with target identified using $Rp_*Rh_*\simeq R(ph)_*$. Then
$$\phi_{h,T_XK}\circ C_{c,K}=C_{c',K}\circ T_Y(\phi_{h,K}).$$
Both equalities hold as morphisms in the $\Lambda'$-module derived categories, with the displayed proper-composition identifications.

proof.text: Put $M=j'_!K$ and $K'=T_XK$. By [lem-sfb-open-extension-zero-constructible-finite-tor], $M$ is in $\Dctf(Z',\Lambda)$, so [lem-sfb-proper-direct-image-coefficient-restriction] applies to $h$ and the open $j$. The inverse-image condition in the statement identifies its Cartesian square with $j':X\hookrightarrow Z'$, $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$, and $h_X=1_X$. Also $K'\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda')$ by [det-prop-scalar-six-ctf]. For either coefficient ring write $u_j:1\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*j_!$ for the invertible unit of the ambient unbounded open adjunction, supplied by [lem-sfb-condensed-open-adjunction-localization].

source.place: Independence paragraph: equality by open restriction, then application of Rp_*

proof.text:
Write $r_{h,N}:j^*Rh_*N\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*N$ for the canonical open restriction [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction], and suppress the canonical tensor/pullback identifications of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1). The exchange map $b_{h,N}$ of [lem-sfb-proper-direct-image-coefficient-restriction] is $r_{h,N}$: since $h_X=1_X$, its unit factor is the identity and $b_{h,N}=j'^*(\varepsilon_{h,N})\circ a_{h,Rh_*N}^{-1}$, where $a_h:j'^*h^*\cong j^*$ is the inverse composition comparison; the counit equation $j'^*(\varepsilon_{h,N})=r_{h,N}\,a_{h,Rh_*N}$ of [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-adjunction-normalization], whose underived adjunct hypothesis is supplied by [lem-sfb-identity-open-underived-square-normalization], gives $b_{h,N}=r_{h,N}$ over both admissible rings $\Lambda,\Lambda'$. The open coefficient square [lem-sfb-proper-direct-image-coefficient-restriction] therefore gives
$$r_{h,T_{Z'}M}\,j^*\gamma_{h,M}=T_X(r_{h,M}),$$
because $h_X=1_X$ and $\gamma_{1,N}=1$ (the defining unit/counit composite in [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image] is the triangle identity). For each open $a$, [lem-sfb-open-scalar-conjugate-normalization] identifies the restriction of the conjugate $\delta_a$ of [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso]: $u_{a,K'}^{-1}a^*(\delta_{a,K})=T_X(u_{a,K}^{-1})\theta_{a,a_!K}^{-1}$, where $\theta_a$ is the K-flat-normalized scalar/pullback identification, the same one that gives [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](1). Suppressing $\theta_a$, this reads
$$a^*\delta_{a,K}\,T_X(u_{a,K})=u_{a,K'}.$$
These equations use the specified comparisons, not arbitrarily chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: Independence paragraph: equality by open restriction, then application of Rp_*

proof.text:
Set $\theta_{h,K}=u_{j',K}^{-1}r_{h,j'_!K}$. By the definition of $e$ as an open-adjunction transpose,
$$\theta_{h,K}\,j^*e_{h,K}\,u_{j,K}=1_K.$$
Let $A=Rh_*\delta_{j',K}\,\gamma_{h,j'_!K}\,T_Z(e_{h,K})$ and $B=e_{h,K'}\delta_{j,K}$. Naturality of $r_h$ [lem-sfb-identity-open-derived-restriction] and the equations of step 2 give
$$\theta_{h,K'}j^*A\,T_X(u_{j,K})=T_X(\theta_{h,K}j^*e_{h,K}u_{j,K})=1_{K'},$$
whereas the transpose identity for $e_{h,K'}$ and the unit equation for $\delta_j$ give
$$\theta_{h,K'}j^*B\,T_X(u_{j,K})=1_{K'}.$$
Both $\theta_{h,K'}$ and $T_X(u_{j,K})$ are invertible. Precompose $A,B$ with $\delta_{j,K}^{-1}$ and apply the Hom bijection for $j_!\dashv j^*$ [lem-sfb-condensed-open-adjunction-localization]; the displayed equality of adjuncts implies $A=B$. This proves the first asserted square in both cases, using only the common inverse-image condition.

source.place: Independence paragraph: equality by open restriction, then application of Rp_*

proof.text: For completeness, the map used above has the required isomorphism normalization. In case (a), [det-sf-comp-coherence-refinement](1)-(2) identifies this exact adjunction transpose with the refinement map and makes it invertible for $K\in\Dctf\subset\operatorname{Loc}(\Dctf)$; the same applies to $K'$. In case (b), [det-nagata-density-normalization-sheaves] gives the unit-induced map $j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*j'_!K$ and its unbounded derived identification, while [sk-lem-nagata-density-normalization] gives the corresponding direct-image identification. Its restriction to $X$ is the identity: restricting the displayed unit and the open base-change identification in the sheaf statement evaluates on the identity map over $X$. The open Hom bijection therefore identifies the restriction-normalized schematic-closure map specified in the item with $e_{i,K}$. This also applies after coefficient change. No density assertion is needed for this closed-inclusion case.

source.place: Independence paragraph: equality by open restriction, then application of Rp_*

proof.text:
Let $P=Rp_*$, $H=Rh_*$ and $N=j_!K$. Under $Rp'_*\simeq PH$, the composition and naturality equations of [det-prop-scalar-six-direct-image](2) read
$$\gamma_{p',M}=P(\gamma_{h,M})\gamma_{p,HM},\qquad
\gamma_{p,HM}T_Y(Pe_{h,K})=P(T_Ze_{h,K})\gamma_{p,N}.$$
Consequently
$$\begin{aligned}
C_{c',K}T_Y(\phi_{h,K})
&=PH(\delta_{j',K})P(\gamma_{h,M})P(T_Ze_{h,K})\gamma_{p,N}\\
&=P(e_{h,K'}\delta_{j,K})\gamma_{p,N}\\
&=\phi_{h,K'}C_{c,K}.
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equality is step 3. This is the second claimed equality, including the specified proper-composition identifications. Only functoriality and reassociation are used after the cited naturality and composition equations.
